subject: english-language
topicDisplay: Unit 1 Writing For Purpose And Audience And Reading To Access Non Fiction And Media Texts
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the best way to structure a piece of persuasive writing for impact?
options: Save the main point for a footnote
Put every idea in one giant paragraph
List random facts in no order
Open with a hook, develop arguments in clear paragraphs, end with a memorable call to action
questions.explain: A strong structure hooks, develops logically and ends with a powerful closing message.

questions.q: Addressing the reader as "you" in a persuasive article is known as:
questions.explain: Speaking straight to the reader using "you" is direct address.

questions.q: A newspaper report only quotes critics of a policy and ignores its supporters. This shows:
questions.explain: Presenting one side while leaving out the other is bias.

questions.q: A leaflet tells readers "Always wear a helmet and check your brakes." Its main purpose is to:
questions.explain: Practical guidance and instructions for the reader's benefit show the purpose is to advise.

questions.q: A writer's TONE in "I suppose, if one absolutely must, one could call this 'art'" is best described as:
questions.explain: The reluctant phrasing and scare-quotes around "art" convey sarcasm and dismissal.

questions.q: A columnist writes: "Of course, some will say the scheme is too costly. But can we really put a price on safety?" This technique of raising and then dismissing the opposing view is:
questions.explain: Acknowledging an objection and then countering it is a counter-argument or rebuttal.

questions.q: Which opening best establishes atmosphere in a piece of descriptive writing?
options: A thick fog curled through the empty streets, muffling every sound.
I will now describe a street that was foggy.
This is a description of a foggy street I once saw.
The street was foggy and quiet and empty that day.
questions.explain: Sensory, image-rich detail immediately builds mood and draws the reader into the scene.

questions.q: A writer's TONE in "Honestly, what a complete and utter shambles this has become" is best described as:
questions.explain: The dismissive phrasing conveys scorn and frustration.

questions.q: In persuasive writing, what is the effect of using a rule of three (a triplet)?
options: It creates rhythm and emphasis, making the point more memorable
It makes the writing harder to read
It removes the need for evidence
It signals the end of the piece
questions.explain: A triplet adds rhythm and emphasis, making ideas stick in the reader's mind.

questions.q: "Do we really want our children breathing this filthy air?" Which technique is this?
questions.explain: It is a question asked for effect, not for an answer: a rhetorical question.

questions.q: Which of these is a FACT rather than an opinion?
options: This is the best film ever made
The film is too long and dull
questions.explain: A runtime can be checked and verified, making it a fact; the others are judgements.

questions.q: When comparing two non-fiction texts, an exam asks about their "viewpoints and methods." "Methods" mainly means:
options: The techniques each writer uses to put their view across
questions.explain: "Methods" refers to the language and structural techniques used to convey the viewpoint.

questions.q: For an article aimed at teenagers about social media, which register is most suitable?
options: A lively, accessible tone with some direct address
questions.explain: Matching register to a teenage audience means engaging but clear, not stuffy or patronising.

questions.q: When asked to identify the AUDIENCE of a text titled "A Beginner's Guide to Filing Your First Tax Return," the clearest clue is that it targets:
options: People doing this task for the first time
questions.explain: The words "beginner" and "first" signal an audience new to the task.

questions.q: Which sentence is the strongest, most memorable ending to a persuasive piece?
options: I think I have said enough now.
That is the end of my writing.
The choice is yours: act now, or watch our future slip away.
So yeah, that's about it really.
questions.explain: A direct, balanced final appeal leaves a lasting impression on the reader.

questions.q: Which sentence opener creates the most engaging, dramatic story opening?
options: My name is Tom and this is my story.
The door slammed shut behind me, and the lights went out.
It was a normal day at school.
I am going to tell you about a time I was scared.
questions.explain: Starting in the middle of the action (in medias res) hooks the reader immediately.

questions.q: "This shameful, disgraceful waste of money makes me furious." The underlined choices are best described as:
questions.explain: Words chosen to stir strong feeling (shameful, disgraceful, furious) are emotive language.

questions.q: You are writing a leaflet for a local charity event. Which feature is most appropriate to the form?
options: Clear headings, bullet points and key details like time and place
A single dense block of text
questions.explain: Leaflets use headings, bullets and signposting so readers can scan key information quickly.

questions.q: When writing to advise, which tone is usually most effective?
options: Reassuring and constructive, offering clear guidance
questions.explain: Writing to advise works best with a supportive, constructive tone that guides the reader.

questions.q: "Over 90% of teachers agree that homework helps." Which persuasive device is used here?
questions.explain: A figure or percentage used to support a point is a statistic.

questions.q: In the persuasive acronym DAFOREST, what does the 'F' stand for?
questions.explain: DAFOREST stands for Direct address, Alliteration, Facts, Opinions, Rhetorical questions, Emotive language, Statistics, Triplets.

questions.q: A travel article says "You will love every breathtaking moment of this paradise." What is its main PURPOSE?
options: To persuade the reader to visit
questions.explain: Positive, emotive language directed at "you" is designed to persuade the reader to go.
